title: SQL agents & workflows
summary: Two ways to go beyond one-shot text to SQL. An **agent** explores the warehouse with tools and queries as often as a question needs. A **workflow** fixes the steps in a LangGraph graph (pick tables, write, run, fix, answer) and lets the model fill each one in. A **data steward** approves queries that read customer data, through an interrupt. Execution accuracy compares all three on the same questions, and the product ships the one the numbers pick.
learn: **A SQL agent**: list_tables, describe_table and run_query (guarded), the glossary in the prompt, assumptions stated
**A SQL workflow** in LangGraph: pick_tables → write_sql → run ⇄ fix_sql → answer, with retries on a conditional edge
**Human approval**: a policy in code, interrupt() in the run node, approve / edit / reject
**Execution accuracy**: compare results, not SQL; strict vs normalized scoring; three systems on one set
flow:
question ─→ pick_tables ─→ write_sql (only those schemas + reference tables in full) ─→ run (guard; customer data → steward) ─┬→ answer
                                                                                      └─(error, tries left)→ fix_sql ─→ run

labs.explain:
Three hard questions through **create_agent** with the SQL tools and the glossary: every tool call and query on the page, checked against trusted answers.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

The same questions through the **workflow** (with and without small reference tables in full) and the agent: right answers and **model calls per question**, and the graph itself.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

Four questions through the reviewed workflow: one runs straight through, three read customer data and are **approved**, **edited** and **rejected** by a scripted steward.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

The 12 evaluation questions plus 3 hard ones through **TextToSQL**, the **workflow** and the **agent**: right answers (normalized and strict), model calls, tokens, latency, and every miss with its SQL.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

path.title: Production path: the SQL workflow, with a steward
path.summary: The product answers SQL questions with the workflow: it sees only the tables a question needs, retries on errors within a bound, reports empty results in code, and pauses queries that read customer data for a data steward. The agent stays available for open-ended exploration, where its extra calls pay for themselves.

steps.title: Workflow
steps.tagline: Fixed steps, the model fills them in
steps.explain: build_sql_workflow: pick_tables (structured output), write_sql with only those schemas and small reference tables in full, run through the guard, fix_sql on an error up to three times, answer from the rows.
production: The number of model calls is known in advance: 3 for most questions, 4 or 5 with a retry.

steps.title: Steward
steps.tagline: Customer data waits for a person
steps.explain: needs_review sends any query that reads the customers table to a data steward through interrupt(); a checkpointer keeps the paused run, and Command(resume=...) approves, edits or rejects it.
production: Use a Postgres checkpointer in production: a review can take days.

steps.title: Agent
steps.explain: build_sql_agent explores with list_tables, describe_table and run_query. It's slower and costlier, and it does arithmetic itself, so keep it for open questions where nobody knows the query shape yet.
production: Module 3's analytics assistant gives the agent governed metrics, so it stops computing rates itself.

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.explain:
The 12 evaluation questions and 3 hard ones (multi-step and a looked-up fact) through all three systems.

| | right answers (15) | hard questions | model calls | tokens | p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TextToSQL (Module 1) | 14/15 | 3/3 | 2.00 | 1,477 | 5.0 s |
| **Workflow** | **15/15** | **3/3** | **3.00** | **1,226** | **7.8 s** |
| Agent | 12/15 | 3/3 | 4.67 | 4,454 | 10.3 s |

The workflow answered everything and used the fewest tokens: pick_tables sends only the tables a question needs, and small reference tables in full. The agent's misses were arithmetic it did itself instead of in SQL: a refund rate worked out from two counts (9.5%, right in words but absent from any query result) and an AOV of ₹2,071 instead of ₹367.07, worked out by the agent from a revenue sum and a row count over order items. TextToSQL's one miss is the weekday the scorer can't read ('0' for Sunday). Strict and normalized scores were equal on this run.
production: Add every question a user found wrong to data/eval/sql_questions.json, with its trusted query.
